clue.text: Branch longs for some bags

definitions.note: bags is British slang for trousers; britches are one kind

parts.note: BR is the standard abbreviation for branch
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A shopper at a branch of some store craves a few bags.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English 'bags' are loose trousers, so the bags here are worn, not carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Britches (breeches) are trousers, which British slang calls bags, so they are some of that clothing.

clue.text: What's close to bust? Eastern bank in Aberdeen

parts.note: a bra is the garment worn right against the bust
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A question about what nearly went bust, followed by an eastern bank in Aberdeen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to bust' sounds like financial ruin, which suits a bank; it is literally the garment close to the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A brae is a Scots word for a hillside or steep bank, so Aberdeen signals the Scottish vocabulary.

clue.text: Pity about keeping bit of distance in Cuban dance

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to rue is to regret or pity
A is a dictionary abbreviation for about

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a small piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of distance

explanation.surface: Regret at keeping one's distance in a Latin dance.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE and A together hold the D.
explanation.definitionFit: The rueda (de casino) is a Cuban salsa danced by couples in a circle.

clue.text: Pasta and rich cake before returning home sick

parts.note: a torte is a rich layered cake

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
synonym

explanation.surface: Someone ate pasta and a rich cake before going home feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortellini are small ring-shaped stuffed pasta, so the general word for that food covers them.

clue.text: Look into Jock's hot, top-class paramours

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

parts.note: het is the Scots form of hot; Jock is a nickname for a Scot
A1 written as AI means first-rate
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Peering at a Scotsman's passionate, high-class lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The look goes into the gap between the Scots word and the top-class rating, which comes from Lloyd's Register of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Hetairai were the cultured courtesans of ancient Greece, mistresses to rich men, hence paramours.

clue.text: Arrival time heading to taxi rank in Paris

parts.note: ETA is estimated time of arrival

indicators.note: the heading of a word is what stands at its head, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of taxi

explanation.surface: Checking the arrival time while heading to a Paris taxi rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxi rank' reads as one phrase, but rank belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: French état means state or condition, including one's station or rank in society.

clue.text: Views reported in destinations for surfers

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: views are sights

explanation.surface: Views at beaches popular with surfers, described in a report.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfers ride the internet, not waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Web surfers browse from one website to another, so websites are where they go.

clue.text: English novelist has me taken aback in places

indicators.note: taken aback literally means carried backwards, so the musical note me inside is turned round

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, English novelists; the MI in the name is the sol-fa note me

explanation.surface: An English novelist who is startled by the speaker in certain passages.
explanation.walkthrough: Me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale; flipping it inside the novelist's name gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim a shot or ball is to place it, directing it at a target.

clue.text: On the threshold military intelligence chaps under control

indicators.note: to chap is to crack or split, so one piece splits the other open and sits inside

parts.note: to keep someone in line is to keep them under control
MI is the abbreviation for military intelligence

explanation.surface: At the start, military intelligence keeps its men in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaps' poses as men but is a verb meaning cracks open.
explanation.definitionFit: In limine is Latin for at the threshold, used of matters raised at the very start.

clue.text: Member lives with relative, lady of the house

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for member
to live is to be, so lives can stand for is
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A club member lives with a relative who runs the household.
explanation.definitionFit: Missis is a colloquial word for a wife or the woman who heads a household.

clue.text: Sewer that could make you sit and retch!

indicators.note: making something means building it out of raw material, here these letters reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sewer so foul it would make you sit down and retch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain, but it is someone who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer, pronounced like sower, is one who sews, which is what a stitcher does with needle and thread.

clue.text: Covered with sunken lines, work in Danube port

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: Ruse is a Bulgarian port on the Danube
a machine that works is said to go

explanation.surface: Heavily lined with creases from labouring in a river port.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugose means wrinkled or ridged, from Latin ruga, a crease.

clue.text: Indigenous Americans having change of heart, right?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, and a change of heart swaps that letter for another

parts.note: the Inuit are indigenous peoples of Arctic North America

explanation.surface: Native peoples altering their views, isn't that so?
explanation.walkthrough: The middle U becomes an N.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is slang for isn't it, a tag question seeking agreement, just like right?

clue.text: Nothing in regatta worked showing evidence of malaise at Oxford

indicators.note: in places the zero within the other letters
worked means kneaded or shaped, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A rower who did nothing at the regatta, looking unwell at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: A regatta is a series of boat races, which fits the Oxford rowing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An aegrotat is a university certificate that a student was too ill to sit exams, proof of sickness.

clue.text: Plant, one occupying a space like this

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, filling it

parts.note: a gap is a space
thus means in this way
an means one

explanation.surface: A gardener placing one plant in a gap, just so.
explanation.walkthrough: AN sits in the space between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Agapanthus, the African lily, is a flowering garden plant with blue or white blooms.

clue.text: Rule divides public on essential point for planner

indicators.note: something that divides another sits inside it, splitting it in two

parts.note: the state is the public body, as in state schools
R is the abbreviation for rule
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A regulation that splits public opinion on the key issue for a planner.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist devises plans and strategy, so a planner is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Crime cases taken by police officer half lost

parts.note: CA is short for cases, as in court law reports

indicators.note: losing half means dropping the first half of the word's letters

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: Crime cases taken over by a detective, half of which are lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is slang for a criminal escapade, especially a robbery.

clue.text: Deliberate gait wrongly shown in French side

indicators.note: shown in means appearing inside something

parts.note: côté is French for side

indicators.note: done wrongly means done out of the proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A careful, faulty stride shown by a French team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' reads as an adjective describing gait, but it is the verb meaning to ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply or ponder, the verb sense of deliberate.

clue.text: Mean chicken cut up on Scottish golf course

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut
Royal Troon is an Open championship course on the Ayrshire coast

explanation.surface: A miserly fowl was chopped up on a famous Scottish links.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicken is the slang for a coward, not a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltroon is an abject coward, a mean-spirited chicken.

clue.text: Herb, one Catholic overlooking a magnificent church

parts.note: basil is a culinary herb
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for Catholic
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Herb, a Catholic, looking out over a splendid church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a grand church given special status by the Pope, so a magnificent church.

clue.text: Shy over flipping Greek coin once

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters are read the other way

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to lob
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Tossing an ancient Greek coin over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, worth a sixth of a drachma.

clue.text: Like a hooker, Patricia grabs Pam roughly!

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Trish is a short form of Patricia

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so the letters are only loosely in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A catfight in which one woman roughly seizes another, behaving like a streetwalker.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampish means like a tramp, slang for a promiscuous woman, so like a prostitute.

clue.text: Two girls needed to carry one vessel

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within

parts.note: gal and lass are both words for a girl
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Two girls are required to carry a single container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a jug, but it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galliass was a large oared and sailed warship of the Mediterranean, a seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Foreign rulers and queen in same ground

indicators.note: in places the royal within the other letters
something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Overseas monarchs and a queen sharing the same territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Ameers, or emirs, are Muslim rulers in the Middle East and Asia, foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Pay one old bill with nothing discounted

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: something discounted is taken off or disregarded, so it is removed

parts.note: a banknote, called a bill in older usage
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Settling an old invoice with nothing knocked off the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police, a distraction here.
explanation.definitionFit: To ante, or ante up, is to put in one's stake or pay one's share.

clue.text: Gale leaving tons in river

indicators.note: when something leaves, it is no longer there, so it is dropped

parts.note: a wester is a westerly gale
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A storm dumping tons of rain into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weser is a major river of north-west Germany flowing into the North Sea.

clue.text: Accepted number till as before almost out of date

definitions.note: out of date marks the word as archaic

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for accepted
N is the abbreviation for number
to ear is an obsolete verb meaning to till or plough

explanation.surface: An agreed figure in the cash register, as before, is nearly expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' suggests a cash register but is the verb to plough; 'as before' flags an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anear is an archaic word for nearly or near, so it means almost in out-of-date English.

clue.text: More talented story-teller needing introduction

indicators.note: needing an introduction means lacking a beginning, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a fabler is one who tells fables

explanation.surface: A gifted narrator who needs to be introduced to the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, meaning more capable or skilled.

clue.text: Spades cut out of flexible present and former sheet metal

indicators.note: flexible means bendable, so the letters can be bent into a new order
something cut out of a word is removed from it

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
taken as written
late means former, as in the late president

explanation.surface: Spades removed from a bendy gift made of old and new sheet metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present and former' looks like a time phrase, but present is the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Terneplate is steel sheet coated with a lead-tin alloy, a kind of sheet metal used for roofing.

clue.text: A term in France for old man

parts.note: per means a, as in ten pounds per hour

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of France

explanation.surface: A French word used for an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' hints at a French answer, which it is, but the clue's own words build it.
explanation.definitionFit: Père is French for father, and old man is slang for one's father.

clue.text: Hard for female in party command that's old-fashioned

indicators.note: one thing for another means one replaces the other

parts.note: a fest is a festive gathering
F is the abbreviation for female
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A firm man standing in for a woman at a party with dated orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Hest is an archaic word for a behest or command.

clue.text: Mammal swimming awhile in great lake tailed

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
to tail fruit is to cut off its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a sea is a great lake of water

indicators.note: swimming suggests things moving about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea creature swimming for a time in a great lake, then followed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sei whale is a large baleen whale, and whales are marine mammals.

clue.text: Some find missing beginner tried hard

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its first letter, and here it is missing

parts.note: strove is the past of strive, to try hard

explanation.surface: A novice who struggled to find something but failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a valuable discovery, so it is some find in the noun sense.

clue.text: Slides and photographs spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means said out loud, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: to shoot is to photograph

explanation.surface: Slides and photographs mentioned in a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slides and photographs' looks like a slideshow, but slides here are playground or water chutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a sloping channel down which things or people slide.

clue.text: Old drudge extremely stupid about taking day off

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read back to front
taking something off means removing it

parts.note: dense means very stupid
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A very dim old labourer taking a day's leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An esne was an Anglo-Saxon labourer or slave, an old word for a drudge.

clue.text: State again: rests are out!

indicators.note: out means disordered or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insistent declaration that breaks are over.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert is to affirm or declare once more, so to state again.
